statusText: CME equity futures are halted for sixteen of the twenty-four published hours, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window, leaving the 22:00Z Sunday restart as the only slot carrying materially elevated conditional risk, and the weekend's escalation now stands verified as intercepted with no reported damage.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is published at Tail 16, still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Saudi Arabia reports no casualties or damage from the intercepted Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh, while CENTCOM puts Hormuz throughput at a six-month high and Aramco returns an estimated 1.0-1.5m bpd of Gulf exports to the market - a weekend whose escalation and supply repair offset each other ahead of the 22:00Z restart
body:
Sixteen of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final eight contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian hours that follow it. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The session was rotational rather than uniform - the Nasdaq added 0.7% while the Dow closed 95 points lower and the S&P 500 rose 0.2% - on a quarterly triple-witching expiry. That divided internal picture is why no structural Tail amplifier is carried into this window: the last observed session was split, not one-way.

The macro backdrop is unchanged and restrictive. The FOMC moved the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September. The H.15 release dated 18 September shows the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the 30-year at 5.29% as of 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%. Against that, VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08% from 15.44 inside a 14.80-15.63 day range and near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range, so the options market ended the week without stress pricing. Crude settled easier for a third consecutive session, WTI at 100.30 and Brent at 103.87, though WTI remains up about 18.85% over the month because the East-West pipeline has been offline since the 11 September strike.

Two verifications separate this run from the preceding one, and both cut in the same direction. First, the Riyadh escalation has been resolved in the reporting: the Saudi-led coalition says the ballistic missile was intercepted and destroyed, the attempts against Yanbu, Bisha, Taif and Farasan were thwarted, and Saudi authorities report no casualties or damage, with the fuel-depot fire near King Khalid International Airport extinguished. This was the first air-raid alert over Riyadh since the July escalation, and the Houthis claim a widened target set, so the event is a genuine escalation of intent - but it is not, on the verified record, a loss of export capacity. Second, the supply-repair side is now quantified rather than rhetorical. CENTCOM reported that Hormuz oil and LNG throughput over the past fortnight was the highest in six months, that primary transit lanes are clear of mines and that more than one billion barrels have moved out of the Gulf in roughly two months. Aramco has sold about 60 million barrels from Ras Tanura for ship-to-ship transfer at Sohar, returning an estimated 1.0-1.5 million bpd of Gulf exports to buyers in China, South Korea, India and Japan. The visible cost of that pivot falls on Europe, which has been told its October allocations are zero and where Dated Brent reached about $130 during the week even as the global benchmarks eased.

A weekend that is escalatory and de-escalatory at once is the classic setup for two-way price discovery at the reopen rather than a persistent one-way path, and under the risk definition used here conflicting evidence lifts Stress ahead of Tail. Stress is published at 28, a step below the previous run, because the escalation is now verified as intercepted without damage while the offsetting supply restoration is documented in volumes. Current Tail stays at the closed-venue floor of 5: no venue is open and no structure has been observed. Confidence is published at 75, one point higher, reflecting two additional primary verifications - the Saudi damage assessment and the Aramco export volumes - against the one input no weekend assessment can hold, a live price path.

No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the published 24 hours. The first Monday catalyst, Goolsbee's remarks at 10:30Z, sits beyond the end of the window, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. One scheduled Asian variable has already resolved: China held the one-year loan prime rate at 3.00% and the five-year at 3.50% for a sixteenth consecutive month this morning, matching all 21 forecasts in the Reuters survey, which removes a potential surprise from the Tokyo hours. Tokyo cash equities open at 00:00Z and provide the first regional cash reference since Friday. Tail is published at 5 through the early halt, drifting up in single steps that track time-to-restart rather than observed structure, reaching a window high of 16 across the restart and its first full hour before easing through the Asian session. Every published hour stays inside the low Tail band and the EA_ON mapping, and no danger window is identified.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first sixteen slots, eased to 4 across the overnight hours and returned to 5 in the final slot. Stress opened at 21, held that plateau through the morning, drifted through 22, 23 and 24 across the afternoon and evening, peaked at 26 shortly after midnight, eased to 25 and stepped up to 29 in the closing hour as weekend escalation headlines landed. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence started at 80, decayed steadily to a 72 trough late in the Saturday session as distance from the Friday tape grew, then recovered into the mid-70s as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Sixteen of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final eight contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian hours after it. Cash closed Friday and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, 18:00 ET. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, beyond its end, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 through the first two hours, steps to 6 from 08:00Z, 7 from 11:00Z, 8 from 13:00Z, 9 from 15:00Z, 10 at 17:00Z, 11 at 18:00Z, 12 at 19:00Z, 13 at 20:00Z and 14 at 21:00Z, then reaches a window high of 16 across the 22:00Z restart and its first full hour before easing to 15, 14, 13, 12, 11 and 10 through the Asian session. That drift tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure and stays inside the low band and the EA_ON mapping for every published hour. Mode is published as event/whipsaw for the restart and the hour after it, then mixed for the first three Asian hours, reflecting expected two-way discovery against a weekend that produced escalation and supply repair at the same time; it returns to normal for the final three hours on the base case that repricing has cleared.
